md_description: This DAG models the experimental and computational workflow for sequencing tumor biopsy samples from cancer patients. It includes tissue extraction and library preparation, sequencing to generate raw read data, and downstream bioinformatic processing to identify somatic mutations and other genomic alterations for personalized oncology analysis.

tumor_biopsy_sample.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included only intrinsic sample identity/origin and baseline biological properties of the biopsied tumor tissue before any laboratory processing. I excluded extraction, library prep, sequencing, alignment, and annotation details because those belong to downstream Process/Capture/Signal/Derivative nodes. I also avoided patient identifiers and experiment identifiers because those are typically defined once at the root Entity level elsewhere, and I did not repeat any already-generated fields. The fields focus on what a user needs to understand the tumor sample itself: specimen provenance, anatomical source, collection context, preservation, and basic pathology-related descriptors relevant to tumor sequencing.

md_schema.descr: Unique specimen identifier for the tumor biopsy sample, as assigned at collection or receipt; example format: TBS-00123. Use this identifier to link the tissue sample to downstream extraction, library preparation, and sequencing records. Do not reuse patient identifiers here.

Biological specimen category for the entity being sequenced; record the sample as a biopsied tumor tissue specimen from a cancer patient before any laboratory processing. Typical values distinguish tissue type and source, e.g. tumor_tissue, metastatic_tissue, or primary_tumor_biopsy.

Anatomical source of the biopsy material at collection, such as lung, breast, colon, pancreas, or other organ/site. Record the site of the tumor tissue before extraction; use the clinical pathology term when available.

Clinical origin of the tissue relative to the patient and disease context, indicating whether the biopsy came from a primary tumor, metastasis, or local recurrence. Record this at the sample level before any processing.

How the tumor tissue was obtained from the patient, for example core needle biopsy, surgical excision, punch biopsy, or endoscopic biopsy. Record the clinical collection method used to obtain the specimen before laboratory processing.
Date the biopsy specimen was collected from the patient, recorded at the time of clinical procurement; use ISO date format YYYY-MM-DD. This is a sample provenance field, not a processing date.

Pre-extraction preservation condition of the tissue sample upon collection or receipt, such as fresh, frozen, or formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE). Record the state of the specimen before downstream laboratory processing.

Estimated percentage of tumor cells in the biopsy tissue before laboratory processing, typically assessed by pathology review; report as a percentage from 0 to 100. This field helps downstream interpretation of somatic variant sensitivity.

Estimated percentage of non-tumor cells in the biopsy tissue before processing, typically based on histopathology review; report as a percentage from 0 to 100. Use when available to describe sample purity/infiltration in the specimen.

Pathology diagnosis associated with the biopsy sample, such as carcinoma, melanoma, glioblastoma, or a more specific cancer subtype. Record the diagnosis assigned to the specimen or linked pathology report before sequencing.

Indicates whether the biopsy specimen was archival material collected previously and later reused for sequencing, versus a newly collected sample for this workflow. Record true for archived tissue and false for newly obtained tissue.

Qualitative description of the specimen condition at receipt before laboratory processing, such as acceptable, compromised, degraded, or insufficient. Use this to capture whether the tumor biopsy was suitable for DNA extraction.

dna_extraction.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included fields only for how DNA extraction was performed on the tumor biopsy tissue: protocol identity, extraction chemistry/kit, operator, input amount, timing, and output yield/quality. I excluded sample provenance and tumor pathology because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded downstream DNA properties that are already represented as the extracted DNA Entity rather than the process itself. I also avoided repeating any root-level identifiers or any fields that may have been generated earlier; the focus here is on process parameters and operational quality indicators needed to reproduce the extraction step.

md_schema.descr: Name of the DNA extraction protocol used for the tumor biopsy tissue, recorded at the time the process was performed; example: Qiagen DNeasy Blood & Tissue extraction workflow. Use the protocol name that was actually followed in this experiment.
Manufacturer or vendor of the DNA extraction kit or reagent system used in this process, recorded during extraction setup. Example: Qiagen, Thermo Fisher, Promega.
Specific kit or product model used for DNA extraction, recorded during process execution; example format: DNeasy Blood & Tissue Kit. Capture the exact commercial kit/model if applicable.

Mass of tumor biopsy tissue input into the DNA extraction process, measured at the time of extraction and reported in milligrams (mg). Typical range depends on biopsy size; use the measured input mass that entered the protocol.

Volume of tissue suspension or lysate input into the extraction workflow, if the protocol uses a liquid input; reported in microliters (uL). Record the actual input volume used at the start of extraction.
Total active duration of the DNA extraction process from start to final eluate collection, reported in minutes. Use the process time actually required for this sample batch or sample run.

Final volume of eluted purified DNA recovered from the extraction process, measured at process completion and reported in microliters (uL). This is a process output quantity describing recovery volume, not a downstream sequencing property.

Total amount of DNA recovered from the extraction process, measured at completion and reported in nanograms (ng). Use the quantified yield from this extraction run, typically from fluorometric or absorbance-based quantification.
Concentration of the extracted DNA eluate at the end of the extraction process, reported in ng/uL. Measure this after purification and elution to summarize extraction output quantity.

Spectrophotometric purity ratio A260/A280 for the extracted DNA, measured after completion of extraction and before library preparation. Typical DNA purity is around 1.8; values outside expected range may indicate contamination.

Optional DNA quality metric describing fragment integrity after extraction, measured on the purified DNA before library preparation. Use the lab-specific integrity scale if available, such as DIN or a comparable quality score.
Person or role responsible for performing the DNA extraction, recorded as the operator at the time of the process. Example: research technician or named staff member.

Whether the extraction completed successfully and produced usable purified DNA for downstream library preparation. Record true when extraction yielded DNA suitable for subsequent processing, false otherwise.

extracted_tumor_dna.reasoning: I revised the extracted_tumor_dna Entity schema to remove fields that collided with already_generated metadata from earlier DAG steps. Because concentration, purity, and integrity were already produced elsewhere in the workflow, I excluded them here even though they are biologically relevant. I retained only non-duplicative entity properties specific to this purified DNA material: identity/linkage to the source biopsy, total mass, storage conditions, aliquot volume, and usability for downstream library preparation. This keeps the node within its semantic territory while avoiding repeated measurements across steps.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the purified DNA entity produced by extraction; example format: DNA-00045. Use this identifier to track the DNA aliquot through library preparation and sequencing.
Identifier of the upstream tumor biopsy sample from which this purified DNA was extracted; example format: TBS-00123. Use this to link the DNA entity back to the original tissue specimen.

Total mass of purified DNA available in this entity at the time it is handed off to downstream processing, reported in nanograms (ng). This is the measured DNA amount after extraction and before library preparation.
Storage temperature for the purified DNA entity prior to downstream use, reported in degrees Celsius. Common values include -20 or -80 depending on the laboratory storage condition at handoff.
Buffer or solution in which the purified DNA is stored, such as nuclease-free water or TE buffer. Record the storage medium associated with this DNA entity.

Volume of the purified DNA aliquot available for downstream library preparation, reported in microliters (uL). This is the actual aliquot volume associated with the DNA entity at the time of use or storage.

Indicates whether the purified DNA entity passed basic acceptance criteria for downstream library preparation, such as minimum concentration and integrity thresholds. Record true if the DNA is suitable for the next process step.

library_preparation.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only how the sequencing library was prepared from extracted tumor DNA: protocol, reagents/kit, input DNA amount, fragmentation/amplification/size-selection settings, indexing/barcoding, and a process-level quality indicator. I excluded DNA identity and purity/integrity fields that belong to the upstream extracted DNA Entity, and I excluded sequencing instrument/capture settings and raw file properties because those belong to downstream Capture and Signal nodes. I also avoided reusing any fields already generated elsewhere in the DAG, including the previously colliding DNA concentration, purity, and integrity fields. The resulting schema focuses on reproducible library-prep parameters and whether the prepared library met acceptance criteria for sequencing.

md_schema.descr: Name of the sequencing library preparation protocol used for the extracted tumor DNA, recorded at the time of the process. Example: Illumina DNA Prep or NEBNext Ultra II DNA Library Prep. Use the exact protocol followed in this workflow.
Manufacturer or vendor of the library preparation kit or reagent system used in this process, recorded during setup. Example: Illumina, New England Biolabs, or Thermo Fisher.

Specific kit or product model used to prepare the DNA library, recorded during the process; example format: NEBNext Ultra II DNA Library Prep Kit. Capture the exact commercial kit/model if applicable.

Mass of extracted tumor DNA input into the library preparation process, measured at the time of setup and reported in nanograms (ng). Record the actual amount of DNA that entered the library prep workflow.
Volume of extracted tumor DNA input into the library preparation process, reported in microliters (uL). Record the actual input volume used for the library prep reaction.

Method used to fragment DNA during library preparation, if fragmentation was performed, such as enzymatic, mechanical, or no fragmentation for already-fragmented input. Record the method applied to the DNA at this step.
Desired average DNA insert size after library preparation, reported in base pairs (bp). Record the target size used for fragmentation and size-selection planning for this library.
Number of PCR amplification cycles used during library preparation, measured as the cycle count applied to the library reaction. Use the actual number of cycles run for this sample.
Indexing or barcode strategy applied during library preparation, such as single-index, dual-index, or unique dual index. Record the strategy used to enable multiplexing in sequencing.
Total active duration of the library preparation process from start to final library cleanup, reported in minutes. Use the actual elapsed preparation time for this sample or batch.
Measured concentration of the completed sequencing-ready library at the end of library preparation, reported in ng/uL. Use the post-preparation quantification value before loading on the sequencer.
Observed average size of the completed sequencing library after preparation and cleanup, reported in base pairs (bp). Measure this at process completion using the lab's fragment analysis method.
Total amount of sequencing-ready library recovered from the preparation process, reported in nanograms (ng). Use the quantified yield from the final purified library material.

Whether the prepared library passed the laboratory quality-control criteria required for sequencing, such as adequate concentration, size distribution, and absence of adapter dimers. Record true if the library was accepted for sequencing.

sequencing_library.reasoning: This is an Entity node for the prepared sequencing library, so I included intrinsic library identity, source linkage, physical/technical properties, and storage state that describe what the library is before capture. I excluded library-preparation protocol, reagent, and QC-process details because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded instrument/capture settings and raw file properties because those belong downstream. I also avoided repeating any already-generated field names or semantically equivalent DNA concentration/purity/integrity fields from other nodes. The fields here are the minimum needed for sequencing setup and downstream tracking of the library entity.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the prepared sequencing library entity; example format: LIB-00027. Use this identifier to track the library through sequencing and downstream raw data generation.
Identifier of the purified tumor DNA entity used to create this sequencing library; example format: DNA-00045. Use this field to link the library back to the input DNA specimen.
Mass of DNA incorporated into the prepared sequencing library entity, reported in nanograms (ng). This reflects the amount of starting DNA used to create the library.
Measured concentration of the completed sequencing library entity before sequencing capture, reported in ng/uL. Use the post-preparation quantification value used for loading or normalization.
Average fragment size of the prepared sequencing library entity, reported in base pairs (bp). Measure this after library preparation and cleanup, before sequencing.
Estimated molar concentration of the prepared library, reported in nanomolar (nM). Record the library molarity used for dilution and loading calculations before sequencing.

Estimated percentage of library molecules containing adapter-ligated fragments in the prepared sequencing library, reported as a percentage from 0 to 100. Use this to describe library completeness before sequencing.
Storage temperature for the prepared sequencing library prior to sequencing, reported in degrees Celsius. Common values include 4, -20, or -80 depending on laboratory practice.
Buffer or solution in which the prepared sequencing library is stored before sequencing, such as EB buffer or low-EDTA TE. Record the storage medium associated with the library entity.
Indicates whether the prepared library entity is ready to be loaded on the sequencing instrument. Record true when the library meets the requirements for sequencing, false otherwise.

ngs_sequencing.reasoning: This is a Capture node, so I included only the sequencing session and instrument configuration: platform identity, manufacturer/model/serial, run setup, flow cell/read geometry, chemistry, loading parameters, and run-level control/QC indicators. I excluded library/sample biological properties because those belong upstream to the sequencing library Entity, and I excluded file properties and read format because those belong downstream to the raw FASTQ Signal. I also used the agent requirement to place hardware manufacturer, model, and serial number here rather than on the Signal. The schema captures what the operator actively configured and what a downstream user would need to reproduce the sequencing run.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the sequencing run/session, assigned when the library is loaded on the instrument; example format: RUN-2026-001. Use this to link the capture event to generated raw sequencing files.
Manufacturer of the sequencing instrument used for this capture event, recorded at run setup. Example: Illumina. Per workflow rules, hardware manufacturer belongs on the Capture node.
Model name of the sequencing instrument used for this capture event, recorded at run setup. Example: NovaSeq 6000 or NextSeq 2000. Include the exact instrument model configured for sequencing.
Serial number of the sequencing instrument used for this capture event, recorded at run setup for traceability. Use the hardware serial number of the active instrument, if available.
Sequencing platform or technology used for the capture event, such as Illumina short-read sequencing. Record the actively configured platform used to read the prepared library.
Type of flow cell or sequencing consumable loaded for the run, recorded at instrument setup. Example: S4, SP, or equivalent platform-specific flow cell designation.
Configured read length in base pairs (bp) for each sequencing read produced by the run. Record the planned or executed read geometry used during instrument operation, such as 2 x 150 bp.
Read layout configured for the sequencing run. Use paired-end when both ends of fragments are read, single-end when only one end is read.
Sequencing chemistry or reagent chemistry used by the instrument, recorded at run setup. Example: SBS v4 or a platform-specific chemistry designation.
Concentration used to load the prepared library onto the sequencer, reported in picomolar (pM). Record the actual loading concentration configured for this run.

Observed cluster density on the flow cell after run setup or completion, reported in thousands per square millimeter (k/mm2) when applicable to the platform. Use the instrument's run metric for this capture session.

Percentage of bases meeting Q30 or better quality for this sequencing run, reported as a percentage from 0 to 100. This is a run-level sequencing quality indicator measured during or after capture completion.
Whether the sequencing capture run completed successfully and generated usable raw data. Record true if the run finished and produced acceptable read output, false otherwise.
Date and time when the sequencing run began on the instrument, recorded at capture initiation. Use the laboratory's timestamp format or ISO-like datetime if supported by the metadata system.

raw_fastq_reads.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I kept only properties of the raw FASTQ artefact itself and removed colliding fields that were already used elsewhere in the DAG, specifically sequencing_run_id and read_length_bp. I retained file identity, storage location, file format, size, read/base counts, technical quality, checksum, compression, and usability because those describe the raw data product rather than capture settings or downstream biology. I excluded alignment and variant-related interpretations because those belong to downstream Process and Derivative nodes.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the raw FASTQ read file or file pair produced by the sequencing run; example format: FASTQ-00091. Use this identifier to track the raw data artefact through downstream processing.
Filesystem path or object-store location where the raw FASTQ file is stored, recorded after generation and during data management. Provide the full accessible path or URI for the file artefact.
Technical file format of the raw sequencing data artefact. For this node the expected format is FASTQ; use the exact file format as stored.
Storage size of the raw FASTQ file, reported in bytes. Measure this after file creation and before downstream processing; use the actual size on disk or in object storage.
Number of sequencing reads contained in the raw FASTQ file or read pair set, counted after file generation. Use the total count of reads available in the artefact.
Total number of nucleotide bases encoded in the raw FASTQ artefact, reported as the sum across reads in bases. Use this file-level dimension to summarize data volume.
Average Phred quality score across bases in the raw FASTQ artefact, computed from the file contents and reported as a numeric score. Use this as a technical quality metric for the raw read data.
Estimated percentage of reads or bases in the raw FASTQ file containing adapter contamination, reported as a percentage from 0 to 100. Use this file-level quality indicator when available.
Fraction of duplicate reads observed in the raw FASTQ artefact, reported as a value from 0 to 1. Use this technical metric to summarize redundancy in the raw data.
Checksum or hash value for the raw FASTQ file used to verify data integrity, such as MD5 or SHA-256. Record the checksum string associated with the stored artefact.
Compression state of the raw read file as stored. Use gzipped when compressed, uncompressed when not compressed, or unknown if not recorded.

Whether the raw FASTQ file passed basic technical validity checks for downstream processing, such as readable format and non-corrupt content. Record true if the file is usable for alignment, false otherwise.

read_alignment.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the computational alignment procedure and software configuration used to map raw reads to the reference genome, along with run-level output quality indicators. I excluded raw read file properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded the aligned file itself because that belongs to the downstream Signal node. I also avoided the previously colliding fields sequencing_run_id and read_length_bp, and I did not repeat any other fields already generated elsewhere. The schema focuses on what a downstream user needs to reproduce the alignment and assess whether it produced usable mapped data.

md_schema.descr: Name of the read alignment software used to map raw sequencing reads to the human reference genome, recorded at the time the process was run. Example: BWA-MEM. Include the exact aligner used in this workflow.
Version of the alignment software used for this process, recorded at run time. Example: 0.7.17. Use the exact version to support reproducibility of mapping results.
Software repository or source location for the alignment tool used in this process, such as a GitHub URL, package source, or institutional mirror. Record where the aligner version came from if known.
Reference human genome assembly used for alignment, recorded during the process. Example: GRCh38 or hg19. Use the exact reference build employed for mapping.
Path or URI to the reference genome FASTA file used during alignment, recorded at process execution. Provide the exact file location used by the aligner if available.
Algorithmic mode or preset used by the aligner for this mapping step, such as default, end-to-end, or local. Record the actively selected mode that affected alignment behavior.
Maximum mismatch or alignment penalty setting permitted by the alignment workflow, recorded as a process parameter. Use the exact value configured for this mapping run when available.
Number of CPU threads allocated to the alignment process, recorded at execution time. Use the actual compute concurrency configured for this run.
Elapsed wall-clock time for the alignment process, reported in minutes. Measure the duration from the start of mapping to completion for this sample or batch.
Percentage of raw reads that successfully aligned to the reference genome, reported as a percentage from 0 to 100. This is a process-level output quality indicator used to judge mapping performance.

Whether the alignment process completed successfully and produced mapped reads suitable for downstream variant calling. Record true if the process finished and yielded usable alignments, false otherwise.

aligned_reads.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I kept only properties of the aligned-read artefact itself, but I removed fields that collide with previously generated names across the DAG: file_path, file_format, file_size_bytes, and duplicate_read_fraction. I retained unique identifiers, provenance linkage, mapping statistics, coverage, integrity, and usability flags, because those are still specific to the aligned-read output and do not belong to the upstream alignment process. I also avoided any capture/software settings and downstream variant interpretation. The resulting schema focuses on the mapped-read artefact characteristics needed by downstream variant calling.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the aligned-read data file or file set produced by the alignment process; example format: ALIGN-00014. Use this identifier to track the mapped-read artefact through downstream analyses.
Identifier of the upstream raw FASTQ file that served as input to the alignment step; example format: FASTQ-00091. Use this to link the aligned-read artefact back to the raw signal.
Number of reads in the aligned-read artefact that successfully mapped to the reference genome. Count this after alignment completion to summarize mapping output volume.
Total number of reads represented in the aligned-read artefact, including mapped and unmapped reads if both are retained in the file. Use this to describe the full content of the aligned data output.

Percentage of reads in the aligned-read artefact that mapped to the reference genome, reported as a percentage from 0 to 100. This is a file-level alignment quality metric derived from the stored mapped-read data.
Average mapping quality across aligned reads in the artefact, computed from the file contents. Use this technical quality metric to summarize confidence in read placement.
Mean sequencing depth across the targeted regions or genome represented in the aligned-read artefact, reported as fold coverage. Use the value derived from the mapped-read file after alignment.
Checksum or hash value for the aligned-read file used to verify data integrity, such as MD5 or SHA-256. Record the checksum string associated with the stored artefact.

Whether the aligned-read file passed basic technical validity checks for downstream variant calling, such as readable format, non-corrupt content, and acceptable mapping statistics. Record true if the file is usable, false otherwise.

variant_calling.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I kept only variant-calling parameters and process-level output quality indicators. I removed the colliding reference_genome_assembly field and avoided any upstream aligned-read properties or downstream somatic-variant entity properties. The schema now focuses on software identity, caller thresholds, compute settings, matched-normal usage, runtime, and call-set acceptance metrics needed to reproduce and evaluate somatic variant calling without duplicating prior fields.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software used to call somatic variants from aligned reads, recorded at process runtime. Example: GATK Mutect2. Use the exact caller employed in this workflow.
Version of the variant-calling software used for this process, recorded at run time. Example: 4.5.0. Use the exact version to support reproducibility of the call set.

Software repository or source location for the variant-calling tool used in this process, such as a GitHub URL, package source, or institutional mirror. Record where the variant caller version came from if known.

Type of aligned input consumed by the variant caller, such as BAM or CRAM, recorded as a process parameter. This describes the alignment input class used for calling, not the file properties themselves.
Minimum base quality threshold applied by the variant caller when considering evidence at a nucleotide position, recorded as a process parameter. Use the exact threshold configured for this analysis.
Minimum mapping quality threshold applied during variant calling, recorded as a process parameter. Use the exact threshold configured for this analysis.
Indicates whether a matched normal sample was included in the somatic variant-calling workflow. Record true when a normal control was used, false when tumor-only calling was performed.
Number of CPU threads allocated to the variant-calling process, recorded at execution time. Use the actual compute concurrency configured for this run.
Elapsed wall-clock time for the variant-calling process, reported in minutes. Measure the duration from the start of calling to completion for this sample or batch.
Number of somatic variants reported by the variant-calling process at completion, including substitutions and small indels if those are jointly called. Use this as a process-level output summary.
Fraction of called variants that passed the caller's filters, reported as a value from 0 to 1. Use this process-level quality indicator to summarize call set retention.

Whether the variant-calling process completed successfully and produced a usable somatic call set for downstream annotation. Record true if the process finished and yielded valid output, false otherwise.

somatic_variants.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only computed-result properties of the somatic call set itself: identity, source linkage, content composition, variant counts, genomic span, confidence/quality metrics, and storage representation. I excluded variant-calling software and thresholds because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded raw or aligned file properties because those belong to upstream Signal nodes. I also avoided the previously colliding field reference_genome_assembly and did not repeat any other already-generated fields. The schema is aimed at helping downstream users interpret the derived variant set and decide whether it is suitable for annotation and clinical integration.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the derived somatic-variant result set; example format: VARSET-00018. Use this identifier to track the computed call set through annotation and reporting.
Identifier of the upstream aligned-read artefact used as input to the variant-calling computation; example format: ALIGN-00014. Use this to link the derivative result back to the mapped-read source.
Total number of somatic variants in the derived call set, including single-nucleotide variants and small indels if both are represented. Record the count after variant calling completes.
Number of single-nucleotide variants in the somatic variant call set, recorded as part of the derived result summary. Use this count when the call set distinguishes variant classes.
Number of small insertion/deletion variants in the somatic variant call set, recorded as part of the derived result summary. Use this count when the call set distinguishes variant classes.

Number of structural variants or larger genomic rearrangements reported in the derived result set, if included by the analysis pipeline. Record the count of events such as deletions, duplications, inversions, or translocations when applicable.
Computed tumor mutational burden from the derived somatic variant set, reported as mutations per megabase (mut/Mb). Calculate this from the final call set when the workflow supports TMB estimation.

Mean variant allele frequency across the derived somatic calls, reported as a fraction from 0 to 1 or as a percent if standardized by the dataset. Use the same convention consistently within the dataset and describe it in accompanying documentation.

Indicates whether the derived somatic variant set contains at least one clinically actionable alteration according to the analysis criteria used in this workflow. Record true when actionable findings are present, false otherwise.
Overall confidence or support score for the derived somatic call set, computed by the pipeline or post-processing rules. Use the lab- or pipeline-defined score that summarizes call reliability.

Whether the somatic-variant derivative passed downstream acceptance criteria for annotation or reporting, based on call-set completeness, confidence, and technical validity. Record true if the derived result is usable, false otherwise.

Storage or representation format of the derived variant set, such as VCF, BCF, or tabular summary, as produced by the computation. Record the exact format in which the derivative is stored or exported.

variant_annotation.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the computational annotation and interpretation procedure applied to the somatic variant results: annotation tool identity, version, data sources, interpretation framework, filtering/classification settings, duration, and process-level output quality indicators. I excluded raw/aligned data properties because those belong upstream, and I excluded the final annotated findings table because that belongs to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided repeating previously generated fields and kept the schema focused on reproducible annotation behavior and whether the process produced a usable clinically interpreted result.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software used to annotate and interpret somatic variants, recorded at process runtime. Example: Ensembl VEP. Use the exact annotation tool employed in this workflow.
Version of the annotation software used for this process, recorded at run time. Example: 110. Use the exact version to support reproducibility of the annotated result.

Software repository or source location for the annotation tool used in this process, such as a GitHub URL, package source, or institutional mirror. Record where the annotation software version came from if known.

Versions of external annotation databases used during clinical interpretation, such as gene models, population frequency databases, and clinical knowledgebases. Record the version string or release identifier for each database used by the pipeline.

Clinical interpretation framework or guideline applied to classify and summarize somatic variants, such as AMP/ASCO/CAP-style rules or a laboratory-specific framework. Record the framework used to convert annotations into clinically meaningful categories.
Classification system used to label variant significance during annotation, such as pathogenic/likely pathogenic/VUS/benign or a similar scheme. Record the exact system used in this workflow.

Threshold used to filter annotated variants for inclusion in the final interpreted result, recorded as a process parameter. Use the exact rule or score cutoff applied by the annotation pipeline when available.

Sources of clinical evidence consulted during annotation, such as COSMIC, ClinVar, OncoKB, CIViC, or a laboratory-curated knowledge base. Record the evidence resources used in the interpretation step.
Elapsed wall-clock time for the annotation and interpretation process, reported in minutes. Measure the duration from the start of annotation to completion for this sample or batch.
Number of variants carried forward into the annotated and clinically interpreted result after applying annotation and filtering rules. Use this as a process-level output count.

Overall confidence or support score assigned by the annotation process for the interpreted findings, computed by the software or post-processing rules. Use the pipeline-defined score that summarizes annotation reliability.

Whether the annotation and clinical interpretation process completed successfully and produced a usable findings set for reporting or integration. Record true if the process finished and yielded valid output, false otherwise.

genomic_findings_table.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only computed output properties of the annotated findings table: identifier, source linkage, row/column dimensions, content summaries, clinical interpretability, and storage/format characteristics. I excluded annotation software, databases, and interpretation rules because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded raw/aligned data properties because those belong upstream as well. I also avoided repeating any already-generated field names or semantic equivalents. The fields here are the minimum needed for a downstream user to understand the table as a reusable clinical genomics derivative and to assess whether it is ready for sharing or integration.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the annotated genomic findings table; example format: GFT-00008. Use this identifier to track the derived table through reporting, sharing, and clinical integration workflows.
Identifier of the upstream somatic-variant derivative used to create this annotated table; example format: VARSET-00018. Use this to link the findings table back to the derived variant call set.
Storage or export format of the annotated findings table, such as CSV, TSV, Excel, or database table. Record the exact representation used for the derived result.
Number of rows in the annotated genomic findings table, counted after derivation is complete. Use this to summarize how many variant or finding entries are included in the table.
Number of columns in the annotated genomic findings table, counted after derivation is complete. Use this to summarize the table's schema width for downstream integration.
Number of findings in the table that were classified as clinically actionable or treatment relevant by the annotation workflow. Use this as a derived clinical summary metric.
Number of variants in the table that meet laboratory reporting criteria for inclusion in a clinical genomics report. Record the count after applying reporting rules.

Indicates whether the table includes clinical evidence annotations or treatment relevance labels for one or more findings. Record true when clinical interpretation fields are present, false otherwise.
Access level assigned to the derived genomic findings table for sharing or integration, such as restricted, controlled, or public. Record the policy applied to this output table.
Checksum or hash value for the annotated findings table used to verify integrity, such as MD5 or SHA-256. Record the checksum string associated with the stored derivative artefact.
Filesystem path, database location, or object-store URI where the annotated genomic findings table is stored. Provide the full location of the derived table artefact.
Whether the annotated genomic findings table passed downstream acceptance criteria for sharing, integration, or reporting. Record true if the derivative is usable, false otherwise.
